text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary cluster 'canary-enc-v2' reporting p99 latency breach (observed p99=4.2s, SLO=1.5s) and multiple streaming stalls. Paging on-call. Impact: canary traffic only.

Maya: seeing the same on dashboards — p95 ~750ms but p99 spike is huge, and streaming sessions show stalls around 3-6s token gaps.

Liam: rolling encoder v2 to 10% traffic ~ 18:41 UTC. Any deployments around that time?

deploy-bot: Deploy initiated: rollout/encoder-v2 -> canary (10%) by arjun at 18:39 UTC.

Arjun: yep that was my rollout. I ran smoke locally, looked fine. I did increase batch window to 40ms to try to improve throughput.

Sam: quick triage: are stalls correlated with specific model shards or specific hosts?

Maya: logs show repeated backpressure events: `KVCacheLockWait` and `encoder-quant-throttle` entries on canary hosts enc-canary-[3-6].

Nora: grabbing `journalctl` of enc-canary-4 now.

Nora: pastebin: https://internal.logs/replay/enc-canary-4/5105001234 — shows spikes in `gpu_mem_pressure` and `enqueue_wait` around 18:41-18:44.

Liam: also seeing higher socket write latencies in the streaming proxies for those hosts. Could batching window bump cause heavier memory pressure + longer tail?

Arjun: I increased batch window to 40ms but kept max batch size same. Might be interaction with prefix KV warmup. I can revert batch window quickly.

Maya: canary still healthy for throughput but tail is the problem. We need to avoid customer-facing traffic. Right now canary only, no customer traffic. But we should rollback to be safe.

Sam: before rollback, can we try quick mitigation: disable long-batching path (set `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8` on canary) to see if tail improves? That avoids full rollback if it's batching parameter.

Arjun: I can flip that in ~2m. Rolling change to enc-canary group.

SRE Lead: alert: page severity set to P1 until p99 < 1.5s for > 15m. Make sure runbook steps logged.

Maya: running query: `select host, p99_latency, stream_stalls from metrics where cluster='canary-enc-v2' and ts between 18:40 and 18:46` — results show enc-canary-4 p99=6.1s, enc-canary-5 p99=5.3s, enc-canary-3 p99=4.0s, enc-canary-6 p99=4.7s. Proxies showing stream stall spikes aligned.

Arjun: change pushed: set `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8` on enc-canary-{3..6}. Watch logs.

Maya: logs after change show immediate drop in `enqueue_wait` but stalls persist for some sessions (less frequent). p99 dropped from 4.2s to 2.8s across cluster. Good improvement but still above SLO.

Liam: any sign of KV cache thrash? Could quant encoder v2 have larger KV usage causing eviction storms under larger batches?

Nora: grep of eviction logs: several `kv_cache_eviction` events at the same timestamps as stalls. evictions spike when batch window is 40ms. Lowering to 8ms reduced eviction rate by ~70%.

Sam: partial mitigation working. If KV evictions are root cause, we need either: 1) revert rollout to encoder v1, or 2) limit concurrency/force smaller batch/adjust quant profile. Which is faster?

Arjun: rollback is fastest and safest. Initiating canary rollback to encoder-v1 now.

deploy-bot: Rollback started: rollout/encoder-v1 -> canary (full) by arjun at 18:47 UTC.

Maya: monitoring metrics — hit refresh. p99 trending down on enc-canary hosts.

Liam: good to capture a few failing request traces for postmortem. Can we dump a couple of streaming sessions that experienced stalls?

Nora: I captured two traces: trace ids `t-enc-5105-01` and `t-enc-5105-02`. `t-enc-5105-01` shows KV eviction mid-request causing recompute of 320 tokens. Attached snippet: 
```
[18:41:12] KV_EVICT key=conv-9876 shard=3 reason=mem_pressure
[18:41:12] recompute:start req_id=abc123 tokens=320
[18:41:15] recompute:end req_id=abc123 duration=3.2s
```

Sam: that recompute matches stall durations. So encoder-v2 seems to increase active KV working set leading to eviction and recompute — hence tail.

Arjun: rollback completed on canary at 18:52 UTC per deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: Rollback finished: canary now running encoder-v1 (100%) at 18:52 UTC.

Maya: post-rollback metrics: p99 back to 1.1s across canary. streaming stalls no longer visible in the window.

SRE Lead: update incident status: mitigated for canary traffic. Keep P1 until we validate full rollout plan and ensure encoder-v2 quant profile fixed.

Liam: we should block any further encoder-v2 rollouts until Arjun updates quantization profile or reduces per-batch KV usage. Add gating in deployment pipeline.

Arjun: agreed — I already created PR #7890 to revert batch window change from default and adjust the quant table to avoid increased KV resident set. Need review from Maya.

Maya: reviewing PR now. Also recommend adding synthetic trace tests that simulate long-context flows to catch recompute behaviour pre-rollout.

Sam: customer impact: since this was canary-only, no customer-facing degradation observed. But if this had slipped into 100% rollout, customers using streaming long sessions would have seen intermittent stalls and timeouts. We should note that in incident notes.

SRE Lead: assign follow-ups: (1) Arjun - update quant profile + tests (PR #7890) due EOD. (2) QA - add long-context synthetic traces in CI for encoder rollouts (ticket #INC-5105-1). (3) Eng-Platform - add deployment gate to block encoder rollouts that increase estimated KV usage > 15%. (4) Postmortem writeup due 48h.

Arjun: ack. Will also add a telemetry flag to detect sudden KV eviction spikes during rollout so deploy-bot can auto-pause.

Nora: packaging logs and traces into artifact: https://artifacts/redwood/incidents/5105001234-artifacts.zip

Maya: final note: great quick response. The `BATCH_WINDOW_MS` flip was a good short-term mitigation but root fix is quant/resident-set.

SRE Lead: handing off to next on-call for postmortem and follow-ups at 19:15 UTC. Handoff notes: mitigated, rollback complete, artifacts uploaded, PR #7890 opened, incident owner Arjun.

Arjun: taking postmortem ownership.

SRE Lead: closing live paging. If anything else flares, reopen thread. :thumbsup:
